title: Deception and ITDR API tokens: OpenAPI scope, token fields, expiry and one-time display

prose.text: This subject covers the Deception and Identity Protection (ITDR) API token pages ([[deception.overview]], [[identity-protection.overview]]). {{openapi-features}} {{itdr-openapi-features}}

openapi-features.statement: Deception supports the OpenAPI specification for the Orchestrate, Miragemaker, Deceive, Landmine, Investigate and Settings features, and API tokens allow decoys to be configured and deployed, event logs and evidence managed, and Miragemaker datasets and personalities configured programmatically.

quotes: Zscaler Deception supports the OpenAPI specification for Orchestrate, Miragemaker, Deceive, Landmine, Investigate, and Settings features.
Programmatically configure and deploy decoys, manage event logs and evidence, configure Miragemaker datasets and personalities, etc.

itdr-openapi-features.statement: ITDR supports the OpenAPI specification for the Endpoint Agents, Threat Detection, Orchestrate, Investigate and Settings features, and API tokens allow event logs to be managed, threat detection policies configured and rules orchestrated programmatically.

quotes: Zscaler ITDR supports the OpenAPI specification for Endpoint Agents, Threat Detection, Orchestrate, Investigate, and Settings features.
Programmatically manage event logs, configure threat detection polices, orchestrate rules, etc.

token-list-columns.statement: The API Tokens page lists each token's Name, Description, Roles (the role assigned), Created By (the ID of the creating user), Created On, Enabled and Status (active or expired).

quotes: Name: The name of the API token.
Description: The description of the API token.
Roles: The role assigned to the API token.
Created By: The ID of the user who created the API token.
Created On: The date and time when the API token was created.
Enabled: Indicates if the API token is enabled or disabled.
Status: Indicates if the API token is active or expired.

token-create-fields.statement: An API token is created with Enabled, Name, Description, a Roles selection and an Expiration in days.

token-expiry-fixed.statement: The expiration period cannot be modified after the token is created and cannot be edited later; a new token must be created after it expires.

quotes: You cannot modify the expiration period after the API token is created. You must create a new token after it expires.

token-shown-once.statement: The generated API token is shown once in the API Token generated window and cannot be retrieved after the window is closed.

quotes: In the API Token generated window, copy the API token.
You cannot retrieve the API token after you close the window.
